facts.text: The executive reviewer, finance reviewer and product liability reviewer are skeptical readers who need different views of the same plan evidence: the executive decides, finance checks the money, and product liability checks what would survive in court.

facts.text: Chapter 13 says the proposal is reviewed by seven critics, including a functional safety engineer, perception engineer, simulation specialist, field test engineer, site operations manager, and the executive, finance and product liability reviewers.
facts.quote: Chapter 13 reviews the proposal through the eyes of seven critics, including a functional safety engineer, a perception engineer, a simulation specialist, a field test engineer and a site operations manager as well as the three named here.

facts.text: Every reviewer should receive a one-page credibility map identifying each safety claim, whether evidence is virtual, physical or mixed, the real data validating the model, remaining uncertainty and who may accept it.
facts.quote: every reviewer should see a one-page credibility map (each safety claim, whether its evidence is virtual, physical or mixed, what real data validated the model, the remaining uncertainty and who may accept it)

facts.text: Reviewers should approve only specific virtual substitutions within a defined envelope, using a validated model to replace a defined physical test, rather than approving virtual testing as a category.
facts.quote: no reviewer should be asked to approve "virtual testing" as a category, only specific substitutions of the form "within this envelope, this validated model may replace this defined physical test"

facts.text: The executive reviewer needs the decision requested, why action is needed now, deadline deliverables and exclusions, probability of meeting the deadline, principal risks, fallback and required resources.
facts.quote: the decision requested, why now, what will and will not exist by the deadline, the probability of meeting it, the principal risks, the fallback and the resources needed.

facts.text: The executive reviewer should challenge money and engineering commitments versus physical-only testing, the minimum useful result, the cost of an incorrect virtual result, the mid-program exam and what happens after September 2027.

facts.text: The product liability reviewer needs jurisdiction-specific compliance analysis, documented standards and editions, supplier and machine-maker authorizations, and a litigation-ready safety case defending every virtual substitution.
